Senior Leadership Team
Senior Leadership Team
At City Academy Whitehawk we have a strong leadership team who work collaboratively with teach other, families, staff and professionals to ensure that children get the very best school experience possible. Our most recent Ofsted inspection in 2024 rated the Leadership & Management (as well as 3 other areas) of the school as Outstanding and we were proud that inspectors noted that 'leaders at all levels share a drive and passion for the school’s mission. The school’s unrelenting pursuit of the best educational offer for pupils is balanced with a focus on staff welfare and well-being'.
If you would like to get in touch with a member of the leadership team, please email the school office on admin@cawhitehawk.org.uk or give us a ring on 01273 681377 and we'll be in touch! We're always keen to hear from families and help in any way we can.
If you'd like to learn a little more about each member of the team, please see their profiles below.
Senior Leadership Team Profiles

Wraparound Care
WRAPAROUND CARE
We operate a free Breakfast Club every day from 8.00am. Children who wish to attend should be dropped at the Canteen gate by 8.10am daily.
Children are offered a choice of cereals, toast and spreads and other breakfast items in a friendly and informal setting.
There is no need to book to come to Breakfast Club, just be at the Canteen Gate between 8.00am and 8.10am to be admitted.
WASP After School Club
We are delighted to be able to provide an extended childcare offer for the end of the day - WASP. WASP after school club runs from 3.15pm to 5:30pm, Monday to Friday during term time (closed on INSET days). Children attending the club are provided with a wide range of activities and the club is run by school staff who are qualified and experienced in play work.
WASP offers a safe, nurturing and inclusive environment for up to 30 children and is operated from the school canteen building.
Sessions include a range of fun activities and play equipment for children to choose from. These include sports and games, arts and crafts, role play, dance and drama, themed days, den building, board games, books, toys, cosy corner, sensory toys, talent shows, trikes and the use of the playgrounds and Trim Trail climbing equipment.
Children attending WASP will be provided with a delicious and healthy snack from a choice of toast, crackers, wraps, crumpets or rice cakes, fruit and vegetables, spreads, juice and water. Vegan options are available every day.
The current charge is £10 per session. Siblings are charged at £7 for the first sibling and £5 for the second sibling.
We are registered to accept payment from Tax-Free Childcare accounts which can provide you with up to £2000 per year towards the cost of using this childcare. A link to sign up for a Tax-Free Childcare account is below and provides further information –
Tax-Free Childcare - GOV.UK
Places at WASP can be booked using the Arbor App. This will enable you to book up to 24 hours in advance providing there are places available. You will only be able to book a place if your Arbor account has sufficient funds available to cover the cost. If you are making payments via Tax-Free Childcare you will need to notify the school office of the reference number for each child you are paying for which will enable us to credit your Arbor account with any funds received.
Do I still have to pay if my child does not attend?
We regret that we are unable to offer refunds for any places that aren’t cancelled without at least 24 hours’ notice. This includes occasions where you child may not attend as they are unwell or need to attend an appointment.
Collection of children
If your child is attending WASP you can collect them at any point between 3.15pm and 6.00pm from the Canteen gate. All children must be collected by an adult – we do not permit children to walk home alone from WASP. There is a £5 late pick up fee per child for any children who are not collected by 6.00pm.
How do I contact WASP?
For further information about WASP please contact Tara Hunt, Team Leader on 07394 140550 or call the school office.

pageCache.text:
CAW Remote Learning
During our partial closure of the school in March through to July of 2020 we worked hard to ensure that children 'off site' had frequent contact with the school team and were taught live online lessons, had access to 'paper pack' homelearning and had access to the necessary materials to engage in school work.
One approach we were very proud to develop in April was our live online teaching on our chosen platform, Electa. We are grateful to The Gatwick School (Aurora Academies Trust) for their help in setting up our online classroooms. The materials from every online live lesson are then made available to download using the links below.
We have worked hard to support families with access to electronic devices and access to our 'paper pack' home learning. Please get in touch for support with either of these.
We have re-enrolled all children in our online 'Electa' classrooms and will be ready to teach an adapted curriculum from Day 1 of any closure. Our White Bubble (Y5/6) tested this contingency plan during a necessary closure in November and we achieved great things together, with children and their teachers working really hard off-site, being hugely successful in their learning!
Our online teaching for all children started again on January 5th 2021. The community is working really hard and engaging so proactively in our learning opportunities. If you need any support in accessing any of our learning offer, please call the office, email us or check the newsletter section of the website.
CAW Online Learning Expectations
So that we can learn online:
I will listen when my teacher is talking. Stay near to your laptop/tablet so that you can hear your teacher.
I will be on time. Get your laptop/tablet ready before your session is going to start. Sit at a table and have some paper and a pencil with you. Your teacher will start at the time you have been given.
I will be respectful. Take turns to speak or ask questions. Click on the raise hand button and wait for your teacher to give you a turn to speak. If you want to answer ‘yes’ or ‘no’ click on these buttons.
I will be kind. Think before you send messages. Is this true? helpful? necessary? kind?
I will be ready for learning. Wear appropriate clothes and try not to have breaks during the session e.g. having a drink or going to the toilet.
If possible please can you wear headphones to help prevent distractions during the lessons!
I agree to these terms and continue to CAW live lessons by

Roundabout Nursery
This page is currently under construction - check back in September for the latest information.
About Roundabout Nursery
At Roundabout Nursery, our aim is to be creative, passionate and inclusive in everything we do.
Working in partnership with parents and carers, we aim to provide an inclusive, stimulating, challenging environment which is a warm, friendly extension of their home.
Children and adults can be creative, have fun together and develop as happy, confident, independent individuals within our community. We welcome children from all parts of the city.
We have specific expertise in supporting children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).
We provide high-quality care and learning for babies and children aged from 3 months to 5 years.
How to reach us
You can use local bus routes 1 and 1a.
We're next door to Best Start Family Hub Whitehawk.
There's plenty of parking for dropping off and collecting children.
Opening times
We're open for 51 weeks of the year.
We're open from 8am to 6pm, Monday to Friday.
Contact Us
01273 681377 - admin@cawhitehawk.org.uk
Our Environment
Indoors
We provide enabling environments for all age groups. Children enjoy creative and sensory activities, where adults follow their lead and intervene sensitively.
We have 3 rooms for 3 age groups:
Each room is spacious and fully equipped to support the children’s learning through play and exploration.
under 2s - Explorers
2 to 3s - Adventurers
3 to 5s - Investigators
Outdoors
We have fantastic gardens for children to explore, come rain or shine. Children are able to access the gardens for the whole of their sessions, and we have wonderful structures and self-selecting resources for them to explore.
We grow fruit and are re-developing our allotment area to grow vegetables as well. Children can pick and eat the things we grow and love helping to tend the allotment.
Our staff
Our Staff
All staff are qualified or working towards their qualification and have a wealth of knowledge and experience of working with children.
We support the council’s apprenticeship scheme, training in-house apprentices who often become staff members when they finish their training.
Key person
We operate a robust ‘key-person’ approach where each child and family has a dedicated worker supporting them with all aspects of their settling, their development and their transitions.
Inclusion
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
We cater for children with a wide variety of additional needs and differing abilities. We're inclusive and passionate about all children we care for.
We have a fully qualified Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Co-ordinator and a SEND Lead Practitioner, who work closely together. Many of our staff are experienced in caring for children with additional needs and some hold SEND qualifications.
We have a specially equipped Sensory Room and a room dedicated for use with children with SEND, where they have small group interventions and one-to-one support.
Inclusion
We are a Nursery of Sanctuary, as part of Brighton & Hove City Council’s City of Sanctuary award.
We were commended for our work with EAL (English as an Additional Language) families and with refugees and asylum seekers.
We have support from the Ethnic Minority Achievement Service (EMAS) and bilingual support for some of our children. We have 19 different languages spoken in our nursery.
Funded Places
About funded places
There are now more ways than ever to reduce your childcare costs. You can benefit from a wide range of funding options depending on your circumstances and the age of your children. To find out more visit Childcare Choices.
We welcome children with funded places including all Early Years Free Entitlement (EYFE) for 9 to 23-months-olds, 2-year-olds and 3 and 4-year-olds.
Two-year-olds with parents in receipt of eligible benefits or tax credits are entitled to 15 hours funding, find out if you're eligible and apply online.
Universal 15 hours Funding for 3 and 4-year-olds.
9 to 23-month olds and 2-year-olds whose parents work can get 15 hours of funded childcare and 3- and 4-year-olds whose parents work can get 30 hours of funded childcare, check your eligibility.
Funded sessions only
If you want your child to have their EYFE-funded hours only these stand-alone sessions can be taken as follows:
EYFE funding for 9 months to 3 years old (working parents)
EYFE funding for 2-year-olds (funded only sessions)
EYFE funding for 2-year-olds (working families)
EYFE for 3 or 4 years olds
Session Times & Nursery Fees
Children under 3 years old - Explorers and Adventurers
£67.58 - for full day, 8am to 6pm, includes breakfast, lunch and tea
£33.79 - for a morning session, 8am to 1pm, includes breakfast and lunch
£33.79 - for an afternoon session, 1pm to 6pm, includes tea
Children aged 3 to 5 years - Investigators
£67.58 - for long full day, 8am to 6pm, includes breakfast, lunch and tea
£50.87 - for short day, 8am to 3:45pm, includes breakfast and lunch
£18.63 - for a morning only, 9:15am to 12:15pm
£26.39 - for a morning session, 8am to 12:15pm, includes breakfast
£18.63 - for an afternoon only, 12:45pm to 3:45pm
£35.34 - for an afternoon session, 12:45pm to 6pm, includes tea
What's included
Included in the prices above are the lunches and teas at a cost of £2.74 per meal.
What's not included
Nappies and wipes are not included in the costs and should be provided by the parent or guardian.
Fees, sessions and holiday
All fees must be paid whether or not your child attends their booked sessions.
There is a minimum requirement of 2 sessions a week.
We need a minimum of 2 weeks' notice for holiday bookings.
Ending your place
If you want to end your place at Roundabout, we need one month's notice in writing to withdraw your child from their place.
Food Provision
We provide breakfast for our early starters. Our lunches and teas are sourced and cooked locally and delivered fresh to us on a twice-daily basis.
We can cater for dietary requirements for diagnosed allergies/intolerances and offer a vegetarian option.
Our menu runs on a 3-week rolling basis and supports healthy choices for children.
Breakfasts are included in the below fees. Lunches and teas are charged as part of the relevant sessions.
Flexible, emergency and occasional childcare
Ad-hoc sessions may be booked subject to availability for children already attending the nursery.
We'll consider each request for occasional or emergency childcare on an individual basis, subject to availability.

Sports Premium
SPORTS PREMIUM FUNDING SPEND 2025-26
Please see our Sports Premium Report in the documents section below.
Funding contributed towards the employment of a PE Specialist who delivered high- quality PE teaching to every class from Years 1–6 for one hour each week, ensuring all pupils received consistent, progressive and engaging physical education. The PE Specialist also provided ongoing CPD and team teaching opportunities for class teachers, improving staff confidence, knowledge and competence in delivering high-quality PE lessons. Regular staff training sessions were delivered to develop curriculum delivery and inclusive practice across the school. In addition, the PE Specialist coordinated a wide range of inter-school competitions and sporting events, ensuring every pupil in Years 5 and 6 had the opportunity to represent the school on at least one sporting trip during the academic year. Swimming provision for Years 3–6 was also organised, enabling pupils to access a six-week block of swimming lessons to develop essential water safety and swimming skills. This investment has significantly improved the quality of PE provision, increased participation in competitive sport, enhanced staff expertise and provided pupils with a wider range of sporting experiences.
Funding was used to provide transport to a wide range of inter-school competitions, festivals and sporting events, ensuring pupils could access opportunities beyond the school environment regardless of financial barriers. Throughout the year, pupils represented the school in football leagues, cricket festivals including events at Hove Cricket Ground, racket sports festivals at Withdean Sports Complex, indoor and outdoor athletics competitions at Withdean and BACA, hockey festivals at Blatchington Mill and leadership events supported by Year 11 Sports Leaders from Patcham High School. These experiences increased pupils' confidence, resilience and enjoyment of sport while allowing them to compete against other schools and experience high-quality sporting facilities. The funding has enabled greater participation in School Games events and supported the development of teamwork, leadership and positive attitudes towards lifelong physical activity.
Funding was used to provide a wide range of after-school clubs delivered by teachers, teaching assistants and external providers, ensuring pupils had access to a broad and inclusive extracurricular programme. Sports clubs included football and dance, delivered by specialist external coaches, alongside a variety of enrichment clubs such as book club, arts and crafts, cooking club and performing arts, led by school staff. This diverse offer enabled pupils with a range of interests and abilities to engage in extracurricular activities, increasing participation, enjoyment and confidence. The variety of clubs also supported pupils' physical, social and emotional development, encouraged healthy lifestyles and provided additional opportunities for children to develop new skills, build friendships and foster a lifelong love of being active.
Funding was used to extend swimming provision across four year groups, ensuring pupils received regular, progressive swimming instruction throughout Key Stage 2. Previously, only Years 2, 3 and 6 accessed swimming lessons; however, this year the programme was redesigned so that pupils in Years 3, 4, 5 and 6 all received a six-week block of swimming lessons. This approach provides greater continuity, allowing pupils to build upon their skills year after year rather than having long gaps between lessons. As pupils have already been accurately assessed and grouped by ability this year, next year's programme can begin immediately with teaching matched to each child's level, removing the need to spend the first lesson on assessment. This maximises teaching time, accelerates pupil progress and ensures children receive targeted instruction to develop swimming competence, confidence and essential water safety skills, supporting more pupils to meet the National Curriculum expectations by Year 6.

The gate will be closed at 08:10. No need to book, just come along and tuck in.

pageCache.pageTitle: City Academy Whitehawk - After School Clubs
pageCache.text:
After School Clubs
What Clubs do you offer?
We have a variety of different clubs that run from 3.15pm to 4.15pm daily and are free of charge. These are run by a mix of external providers and school staff and cover a variety of activities such as sport, reading, Lego and chess. The clubs on offer change three times per year.
In the first week of each term, a letter will go home with all pupils together with a copy of the After School Clubs timetable for that term. The letter will give details of deadlines for bookings, and clubs generally start on the second full week of each term. Details will also be sent out in the electronic Newsletter.
How do I book my child onto After School Clubs?
After School Clubs are all bookable via the Arbor App - all parents/carers have a login, please contact the school office if you are unsure of yours or having problems signing in.
When can I sign them up?
The letter will give details of deadlines for bookings. Clubs are offered on a first come, first served basis and are free for all children.
When do clubs start?
Clubs generally start on the second full week of each term.
How do I know if my child has a place?
When you sign up on the Arbor App your child's place will be automatically be confirmed. When a club is full it will no longer be visible on the Arbor App so you won't be able to book.
Is there a waiting list for some clubs?
Some of the more popular clubs do fill up quickly - please contact the school office who can let you know whether there will be a waiting list operating.
We also offer Wraparound Care from 8am to 5:30pm daily. Please see the Wraparound Care page for more information.
Cookie Policy

Curriculum
Here at CAW, we have used the freedom we have as an Academy to design a curriculum which is broad, balanced, rigorous and provides our children with the skills to become successful learners. Based upon the National Curriculum for England, our curriculum ensures that children benefit from English and Mathematics curriculum rich in aspiration, alongside our commitment to promoting Physical Education and participation in sports of all kinds. All learning opportunities are underpinned by our CAW qualities and a growth mind-set approach to develop resilience and perseverance within our children.
In May 2024, Ofsted commented, 'The school’s carefully sequenced and rigorous curriculum is highly effective. Staff prepare children for the next stages of education, instilling the necessary language and communication skills through enriching activities and opportunities.'
Our humanities curriculum takes children on a journey through time from ancient history up to the modern day. There are three units a year that build upon each other to give children a strong understanding of how ideas and discoveries throughout history have been formed; we teach the skills and knowledge to support children to become geographers through each of these areas of study. There is a strong spiritual, moral and social and cultural focus across our curriculum and it teaches children to be inquisitive, open minded and aware of the impact of a range of civilisations and cultures. Our rigourously crafted timetable enables all subjects to be well taught; maximising this learning time enables all children to demonstrate their personal excellence across the curriculum. We hold a Family Engagement Event at the end of each half term during which all families are invited into school to celebrate this excellence.
We continue to ensure our curriculum is of the highest quality and have written bespoke documents to support our school and wider community. During our most recent visit, Ofsted noted that, 'The school’s ambition for its pupils is reflected in the curriculum design. Staff have carefully defined, rigorous and carefully ordered knowledge. The school has created the curriculum methodically to raise pupils’ aspirations and broaden their horizons. For example, it develops pupils’ learning in religious education to build greater community understanding and fosters a sense of tolerance and respect.'
